newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia beet harvest at 464,000 ha (717,000 in '95).
newsitem.headline: Russia beet harvest at 464,000 ha (717,000 in '95).

text.p: Russia had harvested 464,000 hectares of beets as of October 7, against 717,000 at the same time last year, Viktor Sukhachyov, deputy head of the sugar beet producers' association, Rossakhsvyokla, said on Thursday.
He said the 1996 beet harvest would be at most 16 million tonnes, against an official harvest of 19.1 million last year.
Farmers had harvested 7.393 million tonnes of beets as of October 7, from 45 percent of the 1.015 million hectares sown.
Russian plantings began late this year due to a cold spring and early harvesting was delayed by rainy weather.
Sukhachyov said the harvest could fall below 16 million tonnes. The association revised its estimate down to this level last week.
If the current good weather conditions fail, harvesters will be forced to leave more beets in the fields when winter sets in.
"If the weather changes sharply, that is it starts raining again, the harvest could be lower. It could not be more than 16 million tonnes, but it could be less," he said.
He said sugar content was unlikely to suffer from the longer harvest but harvesters would not be able to gather all the beets in some northern areas before winter.
